descriptionChirho: A sudden, overwhelming rush of water; a flood or torrent used both literally (of destructive waters) and as a metaphor for overwhelming force. All four clusters are the same noun with different prepositions (with, in, for, at). Spanish inundacion/torrente ('flood/torrent'), Arabic tuufaan/sayl ('deluge/torrent'), Hindi baaDh ('flood'), Korean hongsu ('flood'), Swahili mafuriko/gharika ('flooding/deluge'). Uniformly translated as flood/torrent across all languages with no semantic differentiation between clusters.
